=== COLUMN 2 ===
A Look At The Speedway Cars From Topside
a
Armin Krueger Photo
Photographer Armin Krueger came to the track in June with a device used by fruit pickers and electrical
workmen. Lifted some 30 to 40 feet off the ground, Army caught some of the speedway cars in action in the
June 9 150 mile Rex Mays Classic. Here's George Snider of Fresno, Calif. (#11-Thermo-King turbo-charged
Offy) leading Jim Malloy of Denver, Colo. (#27-Jim Robbins turbo-charged Ford). Snider finished eighth and
Malloy was eleventh.
Skidding Loses Precious Time For Winner
Bob Means Photo
Lloyd Ruby of Wichita Falls, Tex., had a slight detour on his road to victory in the June 9 150 mile Rex
Mays Classic here. Near the 100 mile mark, Ruby (#25-Gene White turbo-charged Offy) moved to pass Mario
Andretti of Nazareth, Pa. (#2-Overseas Airways Ford), in the south turn. The smoke from Ruby's skidding
tires reveals that the car was skidding slightly. "Ruby regained control of the car and on the 107th mile passed
Andretti for the lead. Ruby stayed in front for the rest of the way. It was his second victory here. In 1961, he
won the Tony Bettenhausen 200 big car race.

=== COLUMN 2 ===
Famous Sons Of Famous Fathers
Finston
Dan Sheek Photo
Two young men who are relatively new to big time auto racing are Bill Vukovich, Jr. (left) and Gary
Bettenhausen. Bill is the son of the two-time winner of the Indianapolis 500 miler who competed a number of
times at Milwaukee in the early and mid-1950s. Gary's dad, Tony, was one of the all-time favorites of Milwaukee
racing fans. Tearing Tony won 10 major races here — five in stocks, three in midgets and two in speedway cars.
The young men have big pairs of shoes to fill but if they persevere as their fathers did, they are expected to
make their own names in racing. Other famed father and son combinations in auto racing include Billy and
Johnny Garrett, Hank Strube and three sons, Lee and Al Bonnell, Johnny and Johnny Parsons, Jr., Duane and
'Poncho Carter, Clark and Clark Templeman, Jr., Eddie and Joe Russo, the racing Unsers, and Lee and
Richard Petty.

Sellout Crowd Awaits The Big Moment
Bob Means Photo
Part of the nearly 40,000 crowd that crowded into the fair park racing plant await the start of the June
9 150 mile Rex Mays Classic. Pacing the field are Roger McCluskey of Tucson, Ariz. (#8-G. C. Murphy Ford)
and Bobby Unser of Albuequerque, N. M. (#3-Rislone turbo-charged Offy). The winner of the race was Lloyd
Ruby of Wichita Falls, Tex (#25-Gene White turbocharged Offy), who was on the pole position in the fourth
row. McCluskey was out at 24 miles when the magneto broke on his car. Unser was black flagged at 18 miles
when a leak developed in the fuel tank of his car.

Ruby Stalks Andretti For Lead
Armin Krueger Photo
Near the 100 mile mark in the June 9 Rex Mays 150 miler here, Lloyd Ruby of Wichita Falls, Tex. (#25-
Gene White turbo-charged Offy), threw a challenge at Mario Andretti of Nazareth, Pa. (#2-Overseas Airways
Ford). Andretti was leading at the time. Ruby made good on his bid on the 107th mile and won the race.
Andretti finished second. Ahead of them and destined to be lapped was Larry Dickson of Marietta, Ohio (#38-
Jack Adams Lola Ford). Dickson finished sixth.
